title: Gaussian-process priors and finite posterior laws

items.title: The real line with its Borel sigma-algebra is standard Borel
items.statement: The measurable space (R,B(R)) with the usual topology is standard Borel.
items.strategy: Use the countable dense rationals and completeness of the usual metric to make the real line Polish, then apply the standard-Borel definition to the identity presentation.

references.title: O. Biskup, MATH 275D notes, Chapter 2: Kolmogorov Extension Theorem

items.title: A mean and positive-semidefinite kernel define a Gaussian process
items.statement: Assuming AC, for any set T, mean function m:T→R, and symmetric positive-semidefinite kernel k:T×T→R, there is a unique probability law on the cylinder sigma-algebra of R^T whose finite-coordinate marginals are the Gaussian laws with means m and covariances k. Its coordinate process is Gaussian. The construction asserts no sample-path continuity, joint measurability in the index and sample point, or tight Banach-valued law.
items.strategy: First prove the real coordinate space is standard Borel. For each finite index set, construct its possibly singular Gaussian law; the characteristic function gives enumeration invariance and consistency under restriction. Apply arbitrary-index Kolmogorov extension and identify the canonical coordinate process.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of Gaussian priors (2008)
Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning (MIT Press, 2006), Chapter 2

items.title: Finite Gaussian-process posterior and predictive laws
items.statement: Assume AC. For a Gaussian process f with mean m and covariance kernel k, finite observation and test lists, and independent Gaussian observation noise ε~N_n(0,R) with R positive semidefinite, let C=K_XX+R be positive definite. A version of the conditional law of f(X_*) given Y=f(X)+ε=y is Gaussian with mean m_*+K_*X C^{-1}(y-m_X) and covariance K_**-K_*X C^{-1}K_X*. These prior and conditional covariances may be singular. Independent Gaussian prediction noise adds its covariance. The displayed version is defined for every y but, as an RCD, is unique only almost surely. Cholesky triangular solves evaluate the SPD systems without forming C^{-1}.
items.strategy: Stack the finite Gaussian process evaluation vector and independent Gaussian noise, then use the projection definition to show the affine pair (f(X_*),Y) is jointly Gaussian and compute its block mean and covariance. Apply the BCS-03 conditional-normal theorem with observed covariance C positive definite. Repeat with independent prediction noise, and use Cholesky plus forward/back substitution for the numerical solves.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of Gaussian priors (2008)
Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning (MIT Press, 2006), Chapter 2

title: Gaussian-process priors and finite posterior laws — Examples

items.title: A nonzero-mean Gaussian process with correlated observation noise
items.statement: For the constant covariance kernel on three indices, a nonzero mean and a positive-definite correlated noise covariance give a posterior at the third index with mean 16/7 and variance 3/7 after the observations y=(0,1) at the first two indices.
items.strategy: Verify the constant kernel and noise covariance are positive definite or positive semidefinite, construct the canonical Gaussian process and independent noise on a product space, and substitute the exact 2×2 matrices into the finite posterior formula.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of Gaussian priors (2008)
Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning (MIT Press, 2006), Chapter 2

items.title: Singular prior and predictive covariances in Gaussian-process regression
items.statement: A constant-kernel Gaussian process has a singular two-observation prior covariance, while independent identity-covariance observation noise makes the observed covariance positive definite; predicting the same index twice gives a singular conditional covariance.
items.strategy: Use the constant-kernel process, form the observation and repeated-test covariance matrices, verify the observed block is positive definite, and calculate the posterior mean and rank-one conditional covariance.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of Gaussian priors (2008)
Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning (MIT Press, 2006), Chapter 2

items.title: A Gaussian process retains uncertainty at an independent index
items.statement: For the kernel k(s,t)=1 when s=t and 0 otherwise on two indices, observing one coordinate with independent unit-variance noise leaves the other coordinate's posterior law equal to its N(0,1) prior law.
items.strategy: Verify positive semidefiniteness of the equality kernel, construct the Gaussian process and independent noise on a product space, and use the zero cross-covariance block in the finite posterior formula.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of Gaussian priors (2008)
Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning (MIT Press, 2006), Chapter 2
